items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: I studied timpany from a man called Mr. White who worked at -- he worked at Fox studios.

ctx.x: I believe that you have to be prepared for whatever is to come, you know? And when I was telling you when I started freelancing at the studios, then I also started studying, because when you work at the studios, I saw what the other drummers had to do, and I didn't want to be one dimensional.

Now they hired me at these studios because the drummers at the time, that they had, they were legit drummers, you know, they couldn't really play time, so what I was called for was to play what they called the 'traps' -- you know? Play the snare, the bass drum and all of that. But these other fellows, they could roll on their drums and sound like tissue paper tearing, you know, because they were really legit -- they could play all the mallot instruments; they played the marimbas and the chimes and the bells, and…
Do you remember Mr. White's first name?
